Theme

step stool noun

also footstool

classical

Varro, LL 5.168
Cato, Agr. 10.4

scabellum, scabellī n.

noun, second declension

step stool, footstool

Varro derives it from scandere: wrongly, since it is the diminutive of scamnum.

Examples

  • Ad lābrum Theodōrus, in scabellō stāns, pēniculum dentārium, dentifriciō illitum, ipse tenuit

    At the basin, standing on the step stool, Theo held the toothbrush, with the toothpaste on it, himselfLibellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

See also washbasin.

SourcesLewis & Short: scabellum
